rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks what important affair or need is behind the women keeping their sheep away from the water.
rows.anchor: أي خبركما ومخطوبكما أي مطلوبكما

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says khatb is asked about a calamity or someone oppressed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والسؤال بالخطب إنما يكون في مصاب أو مضطهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women mean that they do not water their livestock; the object is omitted because it is understood.
rows.anchor: أي مواشينا , وحذفه للعلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wait until the shepherds leave the water so their flocks will not mix with the men’s.
rows.anchor: عن الماء لئلا يخالطهم - هذا على قراءة أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read the verb in the triliteral form with open yāʾ and damma on dāl; the others use the form with damma and kasra, with a different sense of driving the flock back.
rows.anchor: على قراءة أبي عمرو وابن عامر بفتح الياء وضم الدال ثلاثيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father’s age leaves them to water the flock; their youth suggests they have no brothers who could do it.
rows.anchor: أن لهما أبا , وأن لا إخوة لهما وإلا لكفوهما ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They explain that their father cannot water because of age, and that sending his daughters is not forbidden; propriety varies by custom and circumstance, especially under necessity.
rows.anchor: وهذا اعتذار أيضا عن كون أبيهم أرسلهما لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing their need, Moses helped despite his fatigue and hunger, seeking reward and showing generosity toward the weak.
rows.anchor: انتهازا لفرصة الأجر وكرم الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses withdrew with his back toward the women and rested in shade after serving people, turning his attention to God.
rows.anchor: أي ليقيل تحته ويستريح , مقبلا على الخالق بعد ما قضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses could identify a shady place because places, especially near water, rarely lack something that casts shade.
rows.anchor: وعرفه لوقوع العم بأن بقعة لا تكاد تخلو من شيء له ظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no fault in bringing hardship to the Lord, who is absolutely rich and exalted.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس في الشكوى إلى المولى العلي الغني المطلق نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses emphasizes his request despite his patience to express intense longing and tenderness in supplication.
rows.anchor: أكد سؤاله إعلاما بشديد تشوقه لما سأل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لما attaches the expression of need closely to what God sends, rather than using إلى.
rows.anchor: بالإلصاق باللام دون ( إلى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling provision something sent down and using the past tense generalizes Moses’s need and expresses confidence in God’s promise of provision.
rows.anchor: عبر بالإنزال وعبر بالماضي تعميما لحالة الافتقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun’s resumptive element may be omitted for brevity because Moses was exhausted.
rows.anchor: ولعله حذف العائد اختصارا لما به من الإعياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses needs any good at all, even a small amount; faqīr means severely needy.
rows.anchor: أي ولو قل { فقير * } أي مضرور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Moses was so deprived that eating greens turned his belly green and his weakness made his belly cling to his back.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه كان قد بلغ من الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prophets’ material hardship makes them models: deprivation can preserve and honor the righteous, raise their rank, and teach disregard for this world.
rows.anchor: فانظر إلى هذين النبيين عليهما الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story urges good works, cooperation in virtue, and generous help despite one’s own exertion.
rows.anchor: وفي القصة ترغيب في الخير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said the daughter who recommended Moses was the one who had invited him to their father.
rows.anchor: قيل : وهي التي دعته إلى أبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her distant vocative signals her own smallness and her father’s dignity.
rows.anchor: مشيرة بالنداء بأداة البعد إلى استصغارها لنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She recommends hiring Moses to care for what concerns the household.
rows.anchor: ما يهمنا ؛ ثم عللت قولها فقالت مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She judges Moses strong from his watering work and trustworthy from his modesty and chastity in gaze, speech, conduct, and bearing.
rows.anchor: لما ريناه من قوته في السقي

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls her statement wise and comprehensive: a task is fulfilled when competence and trustworthiness come together.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وقولها قول حكيم جامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father is Shuaib, whom Biqaʿi says the Torah calls Reuel and Yithro, and he supplies pronunciations for both names.
rows.anchor: اي شعيب عليه الصلاة والسلام , وهو في التوراة يسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father emphasizes his wish because a stranger is rarely welcomed eagerly on arrival, especially by a leader.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد لأجل أن الغريب قل ما يرغب فيه أول ما يقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankaḥaka means he will marry Moses to one of his daughters, with the marital bond likened to the joining of the two jaws.
rows.anchor: أي أزوجك زواجا , تكون وصلته كوصلة أحد الحنكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are the two daughters Moses watered; the father lets him consider both and choose one.
rows.anchor: اي الحاضرتين اللتين سقيت لهما , ليتأملهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition can mean either Moses becomes the father’s hired worker or the father sets his own wage or reward at this amount.
rows.anchor: أي تجعل نفسك أجيرا عندي أو تجعل أجري على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijaj is the plural of ḥijja, meaning years; Moses would tend sheep and perform other tasks.
rows.anchor: جمع حجة - بالكسر , أي سنين , أي العمل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ājarahu and ajarahu can refer to hiring or wages; ājarahu can also mean paying the workers their wages.
rows.anchor: وآجره - بالمد والقصر , نم الأجر والإيجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight years are required and completing ten is voluntary; Biqaʿi links these terms to childhood discernment and puberty and the chance to observe a grandson’s character.
rows.anchor: وكان التعيين الثماني لأنها - إذا أسقطت منها مدة احمل - أقل سن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the years ḥijaj is auspicious: they may be blessed through obedience and provision, or each may include pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بما هو من الحج الذي هو القصد تفاؤلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father does not intend hardship in any part of the agreement, obligatory or voluntary.
rows.anchor: أي أدخل عليك مشقة في شيء من ذلك ولا غيره

words: ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father qualifies his promise with God’s will, following pious self-watchfulness, and promises good companionship and faithful performance.
rows.anchor: استثنى على قاعدة أولياء الله وأنبيائه في المراقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses accepts a fair agreement: express undertakings are binding, while the offered extra is gracious generosity.
rows.anchor: على حكم النصفة والعدل والسواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing either eight or ten years fulfills the agreed work; neither party may demand beyond the terms.
rows.anchor: أي أجل منهما : الثماني أو العشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says no one may accuse him of breach; the emphatic negation reflects his broad-mindedness and clean character.
rows.anchor: وكأنه أشار بنفي صيغة المبالغة إلى أنه لا يؤاخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is witness, keeper, and enforcer of their agreement in this life and the next, including marriage, wages, and term.
rows.anchor: أي شاهد وحفيظ قاهر عليه وملزم به في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything people receive is temporary enjoyment of worldly life, whose benefit ends here even if it lasts a long time.
rows.anchor: أي من أي مؤت كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world and all its adornments are neither eternal in the past nor everlasting in the future.
rows.anchor: وهو زينة الحياة الدنيا التي هي كلها فضلا عن زينتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward promised for obedience belongs to the afterlife, which the description of this life as near and low implies.
rows.anchor: مما تثمره لكم المتابعة من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise of reward is wholly trustworthy.
rows.anchor: ومن أصدق وعدا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if people imagine worldly pleasure shares in goodness, what God has is greater, more pleasant, beautiful, and satisfying.
rows.anchor: لأن الذي عنده أكثر وأطيب وأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is everlasting, though it was not eternal in the past, whereas worldly pleasure ends.
rows.anchor: لأنه وإن شارك متاع الدنيا في أنه بم يكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes anyone who avoids the peril of obedience by choosing the greater peril of disobedience.
rows.anchor: فلما بان أنه لا يقدم على خطر المخالفة المذكور خوفا من خطر المتابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse contrasts the person promised a good reward with the person given worldly enjoyment, clarifying their different outcomes.
rows.anchor: سبب عنه وأنتج قوله , مقررا لما ذكر من الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised reward is good because it fulfills the recipient’s hope and endures; God’s promise means it will surely be attained.
rows.anchor: وهو الإثابة والثواب { حسنا } لا شيء أحسن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can remove worldly enjoyment without God’s leave or make it last; it is mixed with troubles, impurities, and sins.
rows.anchor: فلا يقدر أحد غيرنا على سلبه منه بغير إذن منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly indulger is compelled to attend a place he would ransom the earth in gold to avoid; any forced summons brings distress according to its degree.
rows.anchor: أي المقهورين على الحضور إلى مكان يود لو افتدى منه بطلاع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls those who mislead others, block the path, and make excuses about faith and divine oneness.
rows.anchor: ينادي الله هؤلاء الذين يغرون بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners include idols and others whom idolaters treated as divine associates.
rows.anchor: أي من الأوثان وغيرهم ؛ ثم بين أنهم لا يستحقونهذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Followers made leaders partners in practice by obeying them in idolatry, opposing guides, and obstructing their followers.
rows.anchor: وكان الأتباع قد سووا المتبوعين الذين عبدوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment first confronts self-proclaimed partners, then the followers who raised them to that status; followers fear leaders will answer first and worsen their punishment.
rows.anchor: فتشوفت النفس إلى مبادرة الرؤساء بالجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names those deserving punishment instead of simply saying they said, exposing their culpability and self-assumption of divine status.
rows.anchor: قالوا هكذا الأصل , ولكنه أظهر إعلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders point to their followers and say their own adornment and worldly status misled them, although the followers accepted manifestly flawed claims.
rows.anchor: أي أوقعنا الإغواء وهو الإضلال بهم بما زينا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders claim followers chose misguidance as they did; neither group was coerced, despite messengers and reason.
rows.anchor: لم يكن هناك إكراه منا ولا إجبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s revelation to Muhammad parallels earlier scriptures sent to earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك الإنزال الذي أنزلناه إلى أنبيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is the true book in exceptional perfection of composition and discourse, confirming earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: في الحقيقة , لا كتاب غيره في علو كماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some earlier-scripture recipients truly believe, including Abdullah ibn Salam and Mukhayriq; others recognize the truth inwardly yet disbelieve, including Huyayy ibn Akhtab.
rows.anchor: حقيقة كعبد الله بن سلام ومخيريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among Arabs too are true believers and those who inwardly recognize the Quran’s truth from their inability to answer its proof but still disbelieve.
rows.anchor: في الحقيقة والمجاز في المعرفة بالباطن بأنه حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject God’s signs after recognizing them are entrenched disbelievers trying to extinguish the truth’s light.
rows.anchor: أي العريقون في ستر المعارف بعد ظهورها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says denial occurs only after knowledge; al-Baghawi transmits his statement.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : قال قتادة : الجحود إنما يكون بعد المعرفة

words: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Quran, Muhammad had never regularly read any book; the wording denies sustained reading at any time.
rows.anchor: أي تقرأ مواصلا مواظبا في وقت ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min extends the negation over both much and little of the time before the Quran’s revelation.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المراد نفي التلاوة عن كثير الزمن الماضي وقليله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated min emphasizes that Muhammad had read no book at all.
rows.anchor: وأكد استغراق الكتب فقال : { من كتاب } أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad did not habitually write; the verse stresses that his stronger right hand was not used to write a book.
rows.anchor: أي تجدد وتلازم خطه ؛ وصور الخط وأكده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prior sustained reading or writing could have given falsifiers grounds for doubt, but Muhammad had never practiced it enough to gain mastery.
rows.anchor: إذ لو كان شيء من هذه المواظبة في التلاةو أو الخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The falsifiers are those among the People of the Book and Arabs who reject revelation and accuse the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي هؤلاء الذين ينكرون الوحي إليك من أهل الكتاب ومن العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verses establish that worldly life is perishing and transient, so treating it as a source of lasting joy is misplaced.
rows.anchor: ولما تبين بهذا الآيات أن الدنيا مبنية على الفناء والزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative belittles worldly life; calling it the lower life itself supports acknowledgment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فحقرها بالإشارة ولفظ الدناءة مع الإشارة إلى أن الاعتراف بهذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sura urges striving and forbids wrongdoing, the verse mentions diversion first: turning away from it cuts off a source of evil.
rows.anchor: ولما كان مقصود السورة الحث على الجهاد والنهي عن المنكر , وكان في معرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahw is anything that distracts from benefit, such as singing or the adornment of wealth and women, which pleases and excites the soul.
rows.anchor: فإن اللهو كل شيء من شأنه أن يعجب النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Diversion causes heedlessness, forgetfulness, and neglect of reason and what saves one in the afterlife, leading to misguidance; Biqaʿi links this to 31:6.
rows.anchor: فيكون سببا للغفلة والذهول والنسيان والشغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿib gives worldly pleasure, such as dancing after listening; it quickly vanishes because it opposes seriousness and resembles jest.
rows.anchor: وهو فعل ما يزيد النفس في دنياها سرورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Play can mean anything low or false used for amusement and passing time; laʿba can mean a figurine or toy such as chess, and the verb can mean frolicking or treating religion lightly.
rows.anchor: وكل باطل يقصد به زيادة البسط والترويح والتمادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife alone is complete and enduring life, free of death and extinction; al-ḥayawān is an intensive form.
rows.anchor: أي الحياة التامة الباقية العامة الوافية نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensified form and its vowel suggest the movement and agitation inherent in life.
rows.anchor: ولذلك اختير هذا البناء الدال على المبالغة , وحركته مشعرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hereafter pleasures do not end or have low motives; they consist in glorification, knowledge, ease, expansion, intimacy, and delight.
rows.anchor: بل كان ذلك بالتسبيح والتقديس وما يترتب عليه من المعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People mistake both abodes, treating worldly life as permanent and the afterlife as nonexistent, though this world began without life and is mortal.
rows.anchor: فأنزلوا كل واحدة منهما غير منزلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship scene demonstrates the ignorance just described and follows the prior verse’s statement that most people do not reason.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم هذه الآية بما أفهم أنهم لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When danger at sea threatens death, they sincerely call on God alone in heart and speech, knowing no one else can save them.
rows.anchor: إذا أصابتهم مصيبة خافوا منها الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God brings them safely to land, they resume associating partners, admitting their idols cannot save them and exposing their irrationality.
rows.anchor: فصح أنهم لا يعلمون , لأنهم لا يعقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who entrust provision to God neither rejoice at blessings from fear they will be removed nor despair when they depart, but hope for relief and devote themselves to obligatory and voluntary worship.
rows.anchor: فلا يفرحون بالنعم إذا حصلت خوفا من زوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi invokes the saying that awaiting relief is the best worship as a reason for patient trust in provision.
rows.anchor: لأن ( أفضل العبادة انتظار الفرج )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since worrying over worldly wealth neither increases nor decreases it and only hastens toil, spending it in its rights is its true use and investment.
rows.anchor: لما أفهم ذلك عدم الاكتراث بالدنيا لأن الاكتراث بها لا يزيدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give relatives their due first because they have the strongest claim to kindness through maintaining kinship.
rows.anchor: بادئا به لأنه أحق الناس بالبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor person and traveler are included whether or not they are relatives.
rows.anchor: سواء كان ذا القربى أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The due appears voluntary, not obligatory zakat, because other zakat categories are not listed; the poor are included a fortiori.
rows.anchor: والحق الذي ذكر لهما الظاهر أنه يراد به النفل لا الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving is excellent for those seeking God’s face; the guidance applies to everyone following the Prophet, not only him.
rows.anchor: ذلك ليس قاصرا على من خص بالخطاب بل كل من تأسى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts only sincere giving; ostentation forfeits reward, and spending for reputation leaves the giver with loss and burden.
rows.anchor: فهو لا يقبل إلا ما كان خالصا لوجهه لا رياء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere givers are unfailingly successful; those who withhold fail, while ostentatious givers lose wealth and keep its burden.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يشوف فلاحهم شيء من الخيبة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the verb without lengthening, covering giver, receiver, and intermediary; others lengthen it to mean giving.
rows.anchor: في قراءة ابن كثير بالقصر ليعم المعطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riba here is money given to obtain a larger return; Biqaʿi calls this prohibited or disliked, forbidden for the Prophet and disliked for ordinary people.
rows.anchor: مال على وجه الربا المحرم أو المكروه

rows.speaker: المدنيون ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Madinan readers and Yaqub use the form with initial tāʾ, from arba, expressing an increase sought by the giver or recipient.
rows.anchor: على قراءة المدنيين ويعقوب بالفوقانية المضمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase is described as occurring in people’s wealth, hinting the usurer does not truly own what he takes from them.
rows.anchor: فهو كناية عن أن الزيادة التي يأخذها المربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usurious increase does not grow or become pure with God; it is unblessed and ultimately effaced.
rows.anchor: وكل ما لا يربو عند الله فهو غير مبارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi connects usury’s failure to grow with 2:276, where God effaces usury and increases charities.
rows.anchor: يمحق الله الربو ويربي الصدقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The long-vowel reading is agreed and means giving, avoiding any suggestion that the verse encourages taking zakat.
rows.anchor: للإجماع على مدة لئلا يوهم الترغيب في أخذ الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat means charity, named for the purification and increase it brings to wealth, bodies, and character.
rows.anchor: وعبر عنها بذلك ليفيد الطهارة والزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver seeks God alone with full awareness of His majesty, greatness, and perfection.
rows.anchor: خاصا مستحضرين لجلاله وعظمته وكماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Face stands for God’s essence because it evokes reverence and modesty when seen and is the noblest part of the person.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الذات بالوجه لأنه الذي يجل صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular address encourages giving by treating the Prophet as the one who fully understands its merit.
rows.anchor: ولعل إفراد المخاطب هنا للترغيب في الإيتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant demonstrative honors the rare, distinguished givers among the many addressed.
rows.anchor: وبالإشارة إليه بأداة البعد إعلامكا بعلو رتبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere giver’s wealth is multiplied in this life through protection and blessing and in the next through reward from tenfold to beyond measure.
rows.anchor: أي الذين ضاعفوا أموالهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form describes those possessing multiplied increase, like words for someone possessing strength, wealth, fatness, or thirst.
rows.anchor: كما يقال : مقو وموسر ومسمن معطش
